title: Spectral Uniformity Below the Inverse
summary: The inverse function provides the comparison benchmark, but it remains open whether any function has smaller spectral uniformity or none exists, with power permutations as a special case.

formal_statement.body: $\exists F\colon\mathbb F_{2^n}\to\mathbb F_{2^n}:\sigma(F)<\sigma(x\mapsto x^{-1})$ or prove that no such $F$ exists; special case: power permutations.

scope.domain: Spectral uniformity of vectorial Boolean functions over binary finite fields, including power permutations.
parameters: n: extension degree determining the binary finite field
F: candidate function from the field to itself
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether any function has spectral uniformity below that of the inverse or prove none exists, and resolve the special case of power permutations.

citations.label: Pairwise independence of AES-like block ciphers

progress.summary: The source explicitly presents an existence-versus-impossibility open problem. It identifies power permutations as a more approachable special case.
citation_labels: Tim Beyne et al., Pairwise independence of AES-like block ciphers
